neighbours.label: comma (or full stop) that closes a fronted introductory phrase, before the main clause starts
fire: When it comes to choosing a good bicycle for commuting, weight matters less than comfort.
Of all the dishes served at the festival, one stood out for its smoky flavour.
Among the many problems facing small farmers in the valley, water is the hardest.
In the long history of European cartography, few maps were copied as often as this one.
For anyone building a website for a small shop, speed is the first thing to check.
Of the dozens of letters she wrote from the front, only three survived the war.
Across the entire range of modern smartphones, battery life varies enormously.
When it comes to raising money for the school library, parents have been generous.
quiet: Weight matters less than comfort when choosing a good bicycle for commuting.
One dish served at the festival stood out for its smoky flavour and colour.
Water is the hardest problem facing small farmers in the valley this year.
Few maps in European cartography were copied as often as this one was.
Speed is the first thing to check for anyone building a website for a shop.
Only three of the dozens of letters she wrote from the front survived the war.
Battery life varies enormously across the entire range of modern smartphones.
Parents have been generous in raising money for the new school library.

notes: the - pole's top example is also a comma after a fronted clause ('When staying at a hotel,'), so this label may not separate the poles
